figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: the whole chapter hangs on one idea - pressure is the derivative of displacement
figures.read: every result is the derivative, the speed, or the Doppler ratio of one longitudinal disturbance

figures.title: What the speed of sound depends on
figures.why: the dependences are one formula but examiners test each factor separately
figures.data: v = sqrt(γRT/M): v ∝ sqrt(T), v ∝ 1/sqrt(M), independent of P at fixed T
figures.read: raising T raises v; raising M lowers it; pressure alone does nothing at constant T

figures.title: The displacement-to-pressure duality
figures.why: a closed end is a displacement node but a pressure antinode - the most destructive confusion
figures.data: ΔP = -B ∂s/∂x: node of s ⟺ antinode of ΔP
figures.read: displacement and pressure are π/2 out of phase, exchanging roles at every boundary

figures.title: Doppler: what moves, what changes
figures.why: source changes wavelength in the medium; observer changes intercept rate - conflating flips the formula
figures.data: source f' = f v/(v∓v_s); observer f' = f(v±v_o)/v; combined f'(v±v_o)/(v∓v_s)
figures.read: numerator belongs to the observer, denominator to the source

figures.title: Beats: fast carrier, slow envelope
figures.why: two close frequencies produce one audible beat - the identity explains the envelope and pitch
figures.data: f_beat = |f1 - f2|, f_avg = (f1 + f2)/2 from sinusoidal superposition
figures.read: beats count the difference frequency; wax lowers a fork's frequency

figures.title: Triage - name the phenomenon first
figures.why: the first question routes the whole solution
figures.read: the first question names the law; the source/observer distinction is the classic trap
